comparison: Both evaluations support the screening methodology and identification of peptidoglycan hydrolases (C3, C30-C33). OpenEval emphasizes the phylogenetic analysis and bioinformatic approach, while peer reviewers describe it as a 'new strategy' and accept the identification of five enzymes without questioning the methodology.

Both evaluations support the biochemical characterization of pH and salt/urea sensitivity (C51-C52). OpenEval notes these are standard characterization parameters with appropriate citations, while peer reviewers accept the data without raising concerns.

Both evaluations support the mechanistic model based on structural analysis and mutagenesis (C99-C121). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the zipper model and systematic mutagenesis evidence, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the data is 'corroborated by generating variant protein defective in supporting intermolecular bond pairs.'

Both evaluations support the in vivo efficacy data from mouse models (C9, C122-C131). OpenEval notes the complementary evidence from two models and appropriate controls, while peer reviewers affirm the data 'shows promise' and note the study 'demonstrated the safety and efficacy of PHAb10.'

Both address the dual mechanism of action (C56-C69), but with different evaluations. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED through converging structural and functional studies, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting 'some aspects are still unclear' and requesting additional live/dead assays and microscopy to fully validate the mechanism.

Both evaluations support the thermodynamic folding-refolding mechanism (C7, C88-C98). OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of NanoDSF, CD spectroscopy, and domain deletion studies, while peer reviewers affirm the 'temperature-reversible transition from a dimer to a monomer.'

Both evaluations support the crystallographic and structural analysis data (C6, C70-C82). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of crystal structure quality and comparative analysis, while peer reviewers explicitly state 'The crystal structure data is good' and accept the findings without concerns.

Both evaluations support the broad-spectrum bactericidal activity (C41-C50). OpenEval emphasizes the comprehensive documentation across multiple species and growth phases, while peer reviewers affirm the 'broad lytic activity against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria.' Peer result R2 also includes thermostability claims (C4, C37-C40, C53-C54) that overlap with OpenEval R2.

Both evaluations support the exceptional thermostability and bactericidal activity of PHAb10/11 (C4, C37-C40, C53-C54). OpenEval emphasizes this as a key distinguishing feature with strong experimental support, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm these enzymes 'retain significant antimicrobial activity even after prolonged exposure to high temperatures.' Peer result R2 also includes broad-spectrum activity claims (C41-C50) covered separately by OpenEval R3.

Both address thermostability characteristics. OpenEval R2 covers thermostable PHAb10/11 (C4, C53-C54), while peer R3 addresses the contrast with thermosensitive enzymes (C5, C55). Peer reviewers accept the differential thermostability without questioning the findings.

Both address prophage origin and evolutionary relationships (C83-C85). OpenEval supports the prophage prediction and comparative analysis with T4 lysozyme, while peer reviewers accept the phage origin claims and suggest the authors 'correlate their findings with already published findings on T4 lysozyme.'

Both address domain deletion studies (C86-C87), but with different evaluations. OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED as part of the thermodynamic mechanism, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting that findings 'should be corroborated by studying the effect of these holoenzymes/truncated peptides on bacterial cell membranes.'

OpenEval supports the scientific context and rationale claims (C1-C2, C10-C28) as well-supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background and contextual claims.

OpenEval supports the contextual comparisons to prior work and speculation about applications (C132-C144). No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these discussion and comparison claims.

OpenEval rates claim C78 (speculation about missing electron density) as UNCERTAIN, noting the specific reason for missing density is not experimentally verified. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific crystallographic interpretation.
